title: Segmented session minimums and SQ-onboarding credit pilot for Hosted API
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: Large customers running long-lived streaming sessions complain that a flat per-session minimum (e.g., 1k tokens/session) overweights short bursts inside long sessions and creates per-session volatility for conversational SDKs. At the same time, enterprise procurement often stalls due to incomplete security questionnaires (SQs) and lack of clear onboarding credits to offset integration costs. This ticket scopes a combined pricing experiment: introduce segmented session minimums to better align charged minimums with actual sustained usage, and attach a small SQ-onboarding credit that is granted once a customer completes key security milestones (SAML/KMS/audit log review). The experiment tests whether these levers improve conversion, reduce bill volatility, and keep revenue neutral across cohorts.
hypothesis: If we replace a single flat session minimum with a segmented session minimum (a small startup floor followed by lower sustained per-segment floors and pro-rated rolling credits across billing periods) and offer a modest SQ-onboarding token credit upon completing security milestones, then: 1) enterprise trial-to-paid conversion will increase for security-conscious customers, 2) effective billed tokens per active session will decrease for long-lived sessions without materially reducing revenue, and 3) support tickets about unexpected billed minimums will fall by >30% for pilot customers.
experiment_design: A/B cohort test over 8 weeks targeting new and recently-trialing enterprise orgs. Two cohorts: baseline (current pricing: symmetric input/output per-token rates, flat 1k tokens/session minimum) and seg-min (segmented session minimums + SQ-onboarding credit). Segmented rules (seg-min v1): - Startup segment: first 30s or 512 ingress tokens charged against a 'startup floor' of 250 tokens (if actual tokens < 250, bill 250 for that segment). - Sustained segments: thereafter, evaluate each rolling 5-minute window and apply a sustained floor of 100 tokens per segment if actual tokens in that segment are below floor. - Unused sustained segment floor credits can roll forward up to 3 billing periods as 'rolling credits' for the customer (apply to future invoices). SQ-onboarding credit: 10,000 token credit granted once the org completes the security questionnaire AND at least one of the following: KMS integration or SSO/SAML configured. Enrollment: opt-in at org level; require feature flag seg_min_v1. Pricing mapping: retain current per-token rates for both input and output during the pilot to isolate floor effects; measure later sensitivity to asymmetric IO rates. Cohort assignment randomized by org id, target 200 orgs per cohort (n=400).
success_metrics: Primary: 10% relative increase in trial->paid conversion rate for orgs that complete SQ milestones compared to baseline
Primary: <=5% revenue delta between cohorts (revenue-neutral target at experiment-level, accounting for credits)
Secondary: 30% reduction in 'unexpected minimums' support tickets per org in seg-min cohort
Secondary: reduction in bill variance per org (measured as coefficient of variation of monthly billed tokens) by >=20%
Operational: ability to correctly compute segmented floors and rolling credits within billing pipeline with <1% mismatch in parity tests
telemetry_queries: SELECT org_id, cohort, COUNT(session_id) as sessions, SUM(billed_tokens) as billed_tokens FROM billing.stream_sessions WHERE experiment = 'seg_min_v1' AND event_date BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-04-30' GROUP BY org_id, cohort
SELECT org_id, cohort, SUM(support_ticket_count) as tickets FROM support.tickets WHERE tag = 'billing_minimum' AND created_at BETWEEN '2026-03-01' AND '2026-04-30' GROUP BY org_id, cohort
SELECT cohort, AVG(monthly_revenue) as avg_revenue, STDDEV(monthly_revenue)/AVG(monthly_revenue) as revenue_cv FROM analytics.org_monthly_billing WHERE experiment = 'seg_min_v1' GROUP BY cohort
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (now-2w): infra gating, billing pipeline sim tests, security/legal review. Phase 1 (2w-6w): enable A/B for opt-in new enterprise trials; instrument telemetry and dashboard. Phase 2 (6w-10w): evaluate metrics, run parity checks on billing ingestion and credit application, solicit qualitative feedback from pilot customers with Solutions Engineering involvement. Phase 3 (post-10w): if revenue-neutral and support metrics improved, iterate to asymmetric IO rate variants in a follow-up experiment; if not, rollback seg_min_v1 and capture learnings.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: billing engine complexity introduces invoicing errors. Mitigation: run billing pipeline in dry-run mode for a week and surface invoice diffs to finance; require <1% mismatch before live billing. Risk: gaming of startup floor by client-side batching. Mitigation: detect suspicious traffic patterns (many short sessions) and add guardrail that caps crediting benefit for sessions with >80% startup-only traffic. Risk: legal/regulatory pushback on credits carrying forward. Mitigation: legal to review and produce T&Cs for rolling credits and expiration policy.
legal_sq_requirements: The SQ-onboarding credit requires completion of the standard enterprise security questionnaire (link to security questionnaire page) and proof of one of: KMS integration with customer-managed keys, SSO/SAML configured and tested, or attested audit logging setup. Legal will add a short amendment that documents the credit as a non-refundable token credit applied to hosted API invoices and the conditions for expiry. Engineering will expose a secure webhook for Legal to validate SQ completion before granting credit.
required_artifacts: Feature flag: seg_min_v1 implemented and gated (ENG-5522)
Dashboard: sandbox dashboard with telemetry and cohort views (grafana/dashboard/seg-min)
